title: Structural instability and unstable piles
audience: Coordinators, support workers and trained cleaners who may be asked to work in a home affected by hoarding or environmental neglect, as part of an authorised support plan. Not a qualification or authority to clear a property, dispose of a resident's belongings, enter by force, or provide welfare or clinical support.
learningOutcomes: Identify at least three signs that a stack, shelf or floor may fail.
Withdraw, set a boundary and refer the zone without moving the load.
Record the signs, the time and the boundary set.

instruction.heading: Scope of this lesson
instruction.body: This lesson covers recognition and withdrawal. Assessing or altering any stack, shelving or floor is a decision for a competent person. Completing this lesson does not qualify a worker to make that assessment.

instruction.heading: Signs of a possible collapse
instruction.body: Piles, overloaded shelving and damaged floors can give little warning before they fail. Watch for a stack that leans or bows, a cabinet pressing against boxes, shelving that sags or pulls from a wall, staining or softening on the floor beneath a load, and a floor that gives or moves underfoot. Any one of these is enough to withdraw. Do not test a stack by pushing it, and do not climb onto it to look. The signs listed here are recognition cues from this module. No structural standard was read for this lesson.

instruction.heading: Withdraw, set the boundary and refer
instruction.body: Withdraw to a place where nobody is under a load and the exit is clear. Mark the boundary with barrier tape or signage, and keep residents and other workers outside it. Refer the zone for a competent structural or specialist assessment through the coordinator before any load is changed. Record the signs you saw, the time, the position of each load and the boundary you set. Work elsewhere may continue only if it is outside the boundary and the plan allows it.

procedure: Stop. Move everyone out from under and beside the stack.
Observe from outside the no-disturbance boundary. Do not push, lean on or climb the load.
Record the signs: leaning, bowing, sagging shelving, staining or soft flooring.
Set the boundary with tape or signage, and keep people outside it.
Refer the zone to a competent assessment through the coordinator.
Resume only when the competent person has recorded the decision and the plan is updated.

workedExamples.situation: A cabinet leans into a tower of boxes, and the floor shows water damage.
workedExamples.reasoning: Withdraw from the zone. Set a boundary, record the signs and obtain a competent assessment before any load is changed. Issue a stop-work notice and refer for inspection.

workedExamples.situation: A worker wants to move one box from the bottom of a stack to make a path.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Moving a box from the base can change how the stack carries its load, so the worker does not do it without a competent assessment. Stop and wait for that assessment.

equipmentAndPpe: Barrier tape and signage for the boundary.
Stop-work notice template and a sketch of the zone.
Training-only photographs and drawings. No real stacks are approached in this lesson.

commonErrors.error: Moving a stack to make a path, without a competent assessment.
commonErrors.prevention: Withdraw and refer for a structural assessment before any load is changed.

commonErrors.error: Testing a pile by pushing it to see whether it moves.
commonErrors.prevention: Observe from outside the boundary. Do not push or climb.

commonErrors.error: Working under a leaning load because the job is nearly done.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop, withdraw and keep everyone out from under the load.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Assessing and altering unstable structures is restricted to competent people. Completing this lesson does not qualify a worker to do so.
No structural standard or regulator guidance was read for this lesson. Requirements for assessing unstable loads are not stated here.

qualityStandard: The learner identifies at least three instability signs in a described scene.
The learner withdraws, sets a boundary and refers without moving the load.
The learner records the signs, the time and the boundary.
documentationEvidence: Stop-work notice for the zone, with the signs observed and the time.
Boundary record with a sketch of the zone and the people kept outside it.
Referral record for competent assessment, and the decision that followed.
summary: Leaning, bowing, sagging or soft floors mean withdraw.
Do not push, lean on or climb a load.
Set a boundary, keep people outside it and refer.
Resume only on a recorded competent decision.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which observation most clearly requires withdrawal from a zone?
options: A cabinet leaning into a tower of boxes above water-damaged flooring.
A box of books on a sturdy shelf.
A tidy row of labelled crates on the floor.

knowledgeChecks.question: A worker wants to test a leaning pile by pushing it gently. What is correct?
options: Push it gently, because a small push is safe.
Do not push. Observe from outside the boundary and refer.
Push it from the side to see which way it leans.

knowledgeChecks.question: Who decides whether a stack can be altered after the zone is withdrawn?
options: The first worker who arrives on site.
A competent person, with the assessment recorded before any load is changed.

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: This module is training content. It does not grant authority to enter a home by force, to clear, sort or dispose of a resident's belongings without valid consent, to handle or dispose of hazardous waste, to deal with unstable stacks or structural hazards, or to provide welfare, clinical or safeguarding assessments. Completing this lesson does not give a licence, certificate or approval. Work is done only under an authorised support plan and a written agreement with the resident, within the limits set by the employer and the local law. Tenancy, safeguarding and information-sharing rights are jurisdiction-specific, and fire-risk, structural, pest and hazardous-waste decisions belong to the competent authorities and specialists named in the plan. Where authority or consent is unclear, stop and refer.

stopWorkAndReferral.heading: Stop-work and referral rules for this module
stopWorkAndReferral.body: Stop and refer whenever any of these is true: consent is not specific, documented and current; the resident has objected or withdrawn consent; a party seeks entry by force, nonconsensual disposal or removal of personal documents; a fire-load, ignition, egress or obstruction hazard is present; a stack or structure is unstable; pests, unknown liquids or mouldy goods are present; sharps, chemicals or unknown containers are found; waste would go to general disposal without characterisation; private information is requested without authority; or the work would go beyond the approved plan. Stopping is a valid professional outcome. Record the disagreement, protect the resident's choices and refer the authority dispute before any property is moved.
